title: The ridge
logline: The glow, drawn closer than the strip ever went. The woods east of town. The sequence stops before it arrives.

panels.composition: A logging road climbing into the woods east of town, January, fog. WOOD from behind, small, walking up it with BARNABY II. Ahead, through the spruce, the glow — pale, sourceless, filling the fog between the trunks like a second dawn from the wrong direction. The road bends. The page ends before the bend. Every page in this sequence ends before the bend.

image.prompt: a logging road climbing into dark spruce woods in January fog, a man seen from behind walking up it with a small three-legged dog, and ahead between the trunks a pale sourceless glow filling the fog like a dawn from the wrong direction, the road bending out of sight, spare ink and slate watercolor, no panel borders, no words
image.notes: Sixteen pages; none arrives. Reserved: what's there. The strip never asks.

art.line: spare, knowing; economy of line; Era I's black spotting back on purpose in the mill run
art.palette: muted ochres, slate blues, misty sea-foam greens; luminous sunbreaks in the last spring
art.paper: Arches; bristol; the backs of motel registration cards

notes: The Ridge sequence. Stops before the bend, every time.
